name: Patient Corridor
narrativeOnEnter: A long corridor stretches ahead. Numbered doors line both sides — most sealed, a few ajar. A wheelchair sits motionless in the middle of the hall. The fluorescent tubes overhead flicker in and out of rhythm.

hotspots.label: Ward B
hotspots.lockedMessage: A padlocked gate — Ward B. The combination is four digits.

action.text:
An old wheelchair. The leather is cracked and dry. Someone has tied a patient wristband to one armrest — it reads 'PATIENT 07 — WARD B'.

But look closer at the leather band. Scratched faintly underneath the patient number, as if carved with a fingernail over many weeks:

'VOSS, E.'

She scratched her own name onto it. So someone would know who she was.

Tucked into the seat cushion seam, folded to the size of a stamp:

'Dr. Voss —
The chapel bell mechanism controls the maintenance passage.
The tunnel goes east. 200 metres. Hatch at the end.
There is a key in my desk safe.
I'm so sorry it took me this long.
— H'

On the seat, scratched into the leather: 'They don't let us leave.'

Someone crossed it out and wrote below:
'I left.'

WARD B — RESTRICTED ACCESS
Code-Locked Gate

A smaller notice below:
'Padlock combination changed following the 1972 incident.
New code issued to Ward B staff only.
See Patient 07's intake notes for reference.'

In the bottom corner of the placard, almost invisible:
A small stamp. A delta symbol. Δ

The AXIOM mark.

The '1972 incident' wasn't a disturbance.
Patient 07 found a memo from AXIOM describing what the 'therapy sessions' were for.
She named every other patient who'd been mapped.
She walked to Harlan's office and handed him the list.
He had her transferred to solitary that night.
The next day, he changed the gate code.
